To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
co location of corporate units within a chain has no effect on their performance, whereas co located franchised units improve the revenue performance and operational efficiencies of corporate units.
We find that the presence of a co located franchised cousin increases a corporate unit's performance, whereas the presence of a corporate sister has no effect.
corporate ownership and co location of franchised units are complementary, while corporate ownership and co located corporate units are substitutive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the presence of co located same chain firms affects the performance of a focal firm in a multiunit chain.
how the performance of a multiunit chain is influenced by the ownership and co location of units.
how the ownership structure and co location of subsidiaries affect their performance in multiunit chains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results show that co located units of the same franchise chain are more likely to have a positive effect on the revenue performance and operational efficiencies of a corporate owned unit, than a co located sister unit.
the performance of a unit is affected positively by the presence of co located units affiliated with the chain.
the performance implications of co location are contingent upon ownership structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
co location of corporate units has no performance benefits.
the performance of a firm's units is influenced by the ownership structure and the co location of the units in a given market.
the performance effects of co located same chain subsidiaries depend on their ownership structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ownership structure of a multiunit chain affects the nature of interactions among its units and that these interactions influence the performance of corporate units.
the performance implications of co location depend on ownership structure.
firms can improve the performance of their units by strategically placing them with other units of the same firm.
